distraction.heading: How bone grows
distraction.intro: If the lower jaw is underdeveloped, it can be lengthened. The bone is cut, a small device is attached, and the fragments are moved apart little by little. New bone of the child’s own grows in the gap. Scroll down and the device will start working.
distraction.introPro: Mandibular distraction osteogenesis: osteotomy, fixation of a compact distraction device, gradual separation of the fragments and formation of the regenerate. Scrolling walks through the phases.
distraction.note: This is a diagram, not a patient’s scan. The amount and rate of lengthening are planned for each child individually.

phases.title: Surgery
phases.text: The bone is carefully cut and a small device, a distractor, is fixed to it.
phases.textPro: Mandibular osteotomy and fixation of the compact distraction device to the fragments.

phases.title: Pause
phases.text: The device is left untouched for a while: healing begins at the cut.
phases.textPro: A period without activation before distraction starts.

phases.title: Lengthening
phases.text: The device is turned a little each day, usually about a millimetre per day. The fragments move apart and new bone fills the gap.
phases.textPro: Separation of the fragments at a set rate and rhythm; the classic rate after G. A. Ilizarov is 1 mm per day.

phases.title: Rest
phases.text: The new bone matures and hardens. The device stays in place for some time and is then removed.
phases.textPro: Stabilisation of the device until the regenerate mineralises, then device removal.

about.heading: Surgeon at a **pediatric clinic**
about.text: Since 2021 I have worked as an oral and maxillofacial surgeon in the Department of Surgical Treatment of Craniomaxillofacial Anomalies, Pediatric Clinic of Maxillofacial Surgery, Central Research Institute of Dental and Maxillofacial Surgery (Moscow). I operate on children and teenagers: I place mandibular distraction devices, expand the upper and lower jaws, remove jaw cysts and benign tumours, and perform bone grafting. On my blog I show real cases with numbers and terms that make sense to both patients and colleagues.

cases.title: Bilateral microsomia: mandibular lengthening
points: Bilateral involvement: mandibular hypoplasia on both sides and a deformity of the right ear
Complaints: malocclusion, difficulty eating, night-time snoring, appearance
Based on [[plan|3D planning]], curvilinear Conmet [[kda|distraction devices]] with a 50° radius of curvature were chosen
Plan: 15 mm. Considering the patient’s age and growth spurt, [[hyper|overcorrection]] was performed: **[[regen|regenerate]] 21 mm on each side**

cases.title: Distraction instead of orthognathic surgery
points: The patient was a candidate for [[ortho|orthognathic surgery]]
Together with the orthodontist we chose bilateral mandibular [[dist|distraction osteogenesis]] with devices of 70° curvature radius
Plan: 11 mm on the right, 7 mm on the left. Under orthodontic control distraction was stopped early: **7 mm regenerate on both sides**
After finishing orthodontic treatment, orthognathic surgery was **not needed**

cases.title: Left TMJ ankylosis: distraction and coronoidectomy
points: Ankylosis of the left temporomandibular joint. Mouth opening before surgery: 2.5 cm
A second obstacle was a large coronoid process that extended under the zygomatic arch and hit it
In one operation: mandibular [[dist|distraction osteogenesis]] with a curvilinear Conmet R70 [[kda|distraction device]], 20 mm of distraction, and coronoidectomy
Histology: ankylotic masses. After discharge: mouth-opening exercises with a lateral mouth gag
Mouth opening in surgery: 3.5 cm; **at 6 months, at device removal: still 3.5 cm**

cases.title: Mandibular odontoma in an 8-year-old
points: Referred from Tambov with the diagnosis “Benign neoplasm of the left mandibular body. Odontoma? Cementoma?”
[[klkt|CBCT]]: multiple irregular masses within the left mandibular body. The buccal, lingual and inferior cortical plates were intact; the bone bulged on the vestibular side

Surgery under combined endotracheal anaesthesia: the buccal cortical plate was raised as a lid with a piezosurgical approach, **all masses — about 50 — were removed**, the cavity was irrigated with dimethyl sulfoxide solution and closed primarily
Primary teeth over the lesion were extracted for access. The follow-up [[otpg|OPG]] showed **the permanent tooth germs undamaged** and the cortical plate preserved along its whole length
cases.metricCaption: removed in one operation, permanent tooth germs preserved

terms.title: Distraction osteogenesis
terms.text: The bone is cut, and a device then gradually moves the fragments apart. New tissue, the regenerate, forms in the gap between them.

terms.title: Regenerate
terms.text: New tissue that forms in the gap between the separated bone fragments during distraction.

terms.title: Distraction device
terms.text: A compression-distraction device used to move bone fragments apart gradually. Curvilinear devices differ in their radius of curvature.

terms.title: Overcorrection
terms.text: Lengthening beyond the plan, leaving a reserve for further growth of the child’s facial skeleton.

terms.title: Orthognathic surgery
terms.text: Moving the jaws into the correct position in a single operation.

terms.title: Overjet
terms.text: The horizontal distance between the incisal edges of the upper and lower incisors.

terms.title: Osteotomy
terms.text: Cutting the bone. Partial osteotomy comes before device placement, completion after the device is fixed.

terms.title: 3D planning
terms.text: The surgery is modelled on a computer from CT data: the device type is chosen and the amount of distraction is calculated.

terms.title: CBCT
terms.text: Cone-beam computed tomography: a 3D X-ray scan of the jaws.

terms.title: OPG
terms.text: Orthopantomogram: a panoramic X-ray of both jaws.
